title: Combination Sum II
keyIdea: Sort. Backtrack with a for loop from index; each number used once (recurse with i + 1). At one level, skip a value equal to the one just tried (i > index && nums[i] == nums[i − 1]); break when a value exceeds the remaining target.

approaches.name: All subsets, then a set
approaches.idea: Try all 2ⁿ subsets of the sorted array, keep those with the right sum in a set.
approaches.why: Builds every subset, including all the repeated ones.

approaches.name: Sorted backtracking, skip duplicates
approaches.idea: for i from index: skip same-as-previous at this level; break if too big; push, dfs(i + 1, target − c), pop.
approaches.time: O(2ⁿ) worst case, far less with pruning
approaches.why: Repeated combinations are never generated, and too-big values stop the loop.

options: Equal values sit together (for the skip) and big values come last (for the break)
It is required by the recursion

quiz.q: What does i > index && candidates[i] == candidates[i − 1] prevent?
options: Starting the same level with an equal value again, which would repeat combinations
Using a number twice in one combination

quiz.q: Why break and not continue when candidates[i] > target?
options: Sorted, so every later value is too big as well
Each element may be used at most once
